subtitle: How a Princely Court Became a Laboratory of Learning and Steel

panels.shot: sweeping wide shot of a palace morphing into a campus and factory skyline under a dusky sky
panels.action: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV & Sir M. Visvesvaraya stand side by side on a palace balcony, the golden-lit outlines of the Mysore palace blending into university domes, factory chimneys and railway lines stretching into the horizon.

dialogue.text: In an India still ruled by an empire, Mysore’s king and his engineer dreamed of a state that felt like a university and worked like a factory.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य के साये में, मैसूर के राजा और उनके इंजीनियर ने ऐसे राज्य का सपना देखा जो यूनिवर्सिटी जैसा हो, फैक्ट्री जैसा चले।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high balcony onto a council chamber inside the Mysore palace
panels.action: Inside the ornate palace council hall, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV sits poised on a carved throne-chair, young yet composed, while Visvesvaraya, in simple suit and Mysore peta, unfurls detailed papers across a long teak table.

dialogue.text: By 1912, Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV had inherited a quiet weapon: a loyal, educated bureaucracy and a people used to reform, not revolt.

i18n.hi: १९१२ तक, नालवडी कृष्णराज वोडेयार चतुर्थ के हाथ में एक शांत हथियार था – वफ़ादार, पढ़ा‑लिखा अमला और सुधारों की आदी प्रजा।

panels.shot: medium shot over Visvesvaraya’s shoulder showing reports and maps on the table
panels.action: Visvesvaraya stands leaning over the table, finger resting on a map of Mysore marked with rivers, rail lines and shaded districts, as the Maharaja watches, brows knit in thoughtful focus.

dialogue.text: Into this court came M. Visvesvaraya, engineer turned statesman, carrying notebooks from Bombay, memories of floods and famine, and a plan titled not ‘escape’ but ‘Reconstructing India’.

i18n.hi: इसी दरबार में आए इंजीनियर से राजनेता बने एम. विश्वेश्वरैया – बंबई की डायरी, बाढ़‑क़हत की यादें, और ‘भागना’ नहीं, ‘रिकन्स्ट्रक्टिंग इंडिया’ नाम की योजना लेकर।

panels.shot: close-up on Visvesvaraya’s calm yet intense face, light from a window catching his eyes
panels.action: Visvesvaraya’s face is shown in close-up, lit from one side by morning light through a jaali, his expression firm, lips slightly parted as he addresses the unseen council.

dialogue.speaker: M. Visvesvaraya
dialogue.text: Your Highness, a modern state must think as a school, bank and workshop together.

i18n.hi: महाराज, आधुनिक राज्य को स्कूल, बैंक और वर्कशॉप – तीनों की तरह साथ‑साथ सोचना होगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of the council chamber with a few anonymous advisors faintly in the background
panels.action: The Maharaja sits forward, one hand resting on the armrest, the other lightly touching a pile of petitions and budget documents, as two shadowed officials watch the exchange from a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Mysore was rich in forests, silk and sandalwood, but its people sent sons away for study, its savings flowed through British banks, and its wealth left the state as raw produce.

i18n.hi: मैसूर के जंगल, रेशम और चंदन ने धन तो दिया, पर बेटे पढ़ने बाहर जाते, बचतें ब्रिटिश बैंकों में जातीं, और दौलत कच्चे माल की तरह राज्य से बाहर बहती रही।

panels.shot: overhead shot of Mysore city showing palace, narrow streets, and an older college building
panels.action: From above, tiled roofs and temple gopurams crowd around the palace; in one corner, a modest college building with a playground is visible, its verandah filled with students in simple white clothes.

dialogue.text: Colleges stood in Mysore already, tied to Madras University and British-controlled examinations far away in the provinces.

i18n.hi: कॉलज थे, पर मैसूर के नहीं – मद्रास यूनिवर्सिटी से बंधे, दूर सूबों में बैठे अंग्रेज़ परीक्षक उन्हें चलाते थे।

panels.shot: interior shot of a small college classroom, students bent over papers
panels.action: A cramped classroom shows young men seated at wooden benches writing by lamplight, a tired teacher watching as a peon carries a sealed packet of exam papers marked for dispatch to Madras.

dialogue.text: If Mysore wanted to direct its own future, it needed not only classrooms but a university under its own law and seal.

i18n.hi: अपना भविष्य खुद लिखना है, तो सिर्फ़ क्लासरूम नहीं, अपना क़ानून और मुहर वाली यूनिवर्सिटी चाहिए।

panels.shot: medium shot inside palace library, both figures standing among shelves and rolled plans
panels.action: In a quiet palace library lined with books and framed portraits, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Visvesvaraya stand by a large desk covered with a draft Act, quill pens and bound reports from universities across India and Europe.

dialogue.speaker: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: Let us give Mysore a university by Mysore law—if we can carry the burden honestly.

i18n.hi: आइए मैसूर को मैसूर के क़ानून से यूनिवर्सिटी दें – बशर्ते हम उसका बोझ ईमानदारी से उठा सकें।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot of a formal durbar where the Act is being assented to
panels.action: In a ceremonial hall, the Maharaja sits formally robed as a senior official kneels presenting the rolled University of Mysore Act; Visvesvaraya stands slightly behind, hands folded, watching the moment with restrained satisfaction.

dialogue.text: In 1916, the Government of Mysore passed the University of Mysore Act, founding the first university in an Indian princely state, outside the British-administered provinces.

i18n.hi: १९१६ में मैसूर सरकार ने यूनिवर्सिटी ऑफ मैसूर एक्ट पास किया – रियासतों में बनी पहली यूनिवर्सिटी, प्रांतों से बाहर, भारतीय ज़मीन पर।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the new university buildings amid fields and trees
panels.action: Newly built university buildings, with red-tiled roofs and broad verandahs, rise amid open fields; students walk in small groups along a path, carrying books and umbrellas under a mild sun.

dialogue.text: On the hill at Mysore, lecture halls and laboratories rose; a senate of teachers and officials began framing rules for courses from Sanskrit to science.

i18n.hi: मैसूर की टेकरी पर लेक्चर हॉल और लैबें उठीं; प्रोफेसरों और अफ़सरों की सेनेट ने संस्कृत से साइंस तक के नए कोर्स की रूपरेखा बाँधी।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a science laboratory, students gathered around equipment
panels.action: Inside a simple laboratory, students in white dhotis and coats crowd around glass beakers and balances, as an instructor gestures towards a blackboard filled with diagrams of pulleys and chemical symbols.

dialogue.text: By Mysore’s own statute, examinations and degrees could now be shaped to its needs, feeding men and women into schools, offices and soon, into factories.

i18n.hi: अब मैसूर के अपने क़ानून से इम्तिहान और डिग्रियाँ उसकी ज़रूरत के मुताबिक़ ढलने लगीं – स्कूलों, दफ़्तरों और जल्द ही फ़ैक्ट्रियों के लिए औरत‑मर्द तैयार होने लगे।

panels.shot: split-screen style composition: one half shows a classroom, the other a workshop floor plan on a table
panels.action: On one side of the panel, a professor writes on a chalkboard for attentive students; on the other, Visvesvaraya spreads a blueprint of a factory across a table as the Maharaja watches, the line of the split aligning the chalkboard with the blueprint.

dialogue.text: But knowledge without work remains paper. Visvesvaraya’s eye moved from classrooms to machines, from degrees to demand.

i18n.hi: पर सिर्फ़ किताबों से काम नहीं चलता; बिना मेहनत के ज्ञान कागज़ ही रहता है। विश्वेश्वरैया की नज़र क्लासरूम से मशीनों पर, डिग्री से मांग पर गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of a sandalwood forest with workers and carts
panels.action: In a dense sandalwood forest, workers load fragrant logs onto ox-carts; a supervising official notes figures in a ledger as mist filters through the trees.

dialogue.text: For generations, Mysore’s sandalwood went out as logs. The profit travelled away with the scent.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से मैसूर का चंदन लकड़ी बनकर बाहर जाता रहा; मुनाफ़ा खुशबू की तरह दूर उड़ जाता था।

panels.shot: interior shot of palace office, maps and charts on walls, focus on sandalwood export figures
panels.action: Back in a palace office, Visvesvaraya points to a chart showing rising export numbers and low returns for Mysore, while the Maharaja studies the graph, chin resting on one hand.

dialogue.speaker: M. Visvesvaraya
dialogue.text: We must export less timber and more thought. Oil and soap, not only logs.

i18n.hi: हमें कम लकड़ी, ज़्यादा सोच बेचनी है – सिर्फ़ लट्ठ नहीं, तेल और साबुन भी।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of the Government Sandalwood Oil Factory under construction
panels.action: A newly built factory complex stands outside Mysore city, scaffolding still on one wing; workers haul metal parts while a tall chimney towers over tiled roofs and a narrow-gauge track runs nearby.

dialogue.text: In 1916, the Government Sandalwood Oil Factory began to take shape, distilling Mysore’s forests into carefully measured essence under state control.

i18n.hi: १९१६ में सरकारी सैंडलवुड ऑयल फ़ैक्ट्री की नींव पड़ी – मैसूर के जंगलों को नाप‑तौल कर, राज्य की नज़र में, सुगंधी तेल में बदला गया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of distillation hall with equipment
panels.action: Inside the factory, workers in simple uniforms operate gleaming distillation vessels; steam rises in soft clouds as an overseer checks gauges and notes readings in a bound register.

dialogue.text: Here, chemistry and administration met. Yields, costs and wastage were recorded line by line, turning a forest into an industry.

i18n.hi: यहीं रसायन और प्रशासन मिले – हर उपज, ख़र्च और बर्बादी लाइन दर लाइन दर्ज हुई; जंगल धीरे‑धीरे उद्योग में बदल गया।

panels.shot: close-up of a worker pouring sandalwood oil into a labelled container
panels.action: A worker carefully tips a gleaming stream of pale oil into a metal container, his hands steady, the background showing neatly stacked canisters stamped with the Mysore state emblem.

dialogue.text: Within two years, in 1918, that oil would be shaped into Mysore Sandal Soap, a state-branded value added to every drop.

i18n.hi: सिर्फ़ दो साल में, १९१८ में, उसी तेल ने आकार लिया – मैसूर सैंडल सोप, हर बूंद में राज्य की मुहर लगा हुआ मूल्य।

panels.shot: wide shot of a small soap workshop line with moulds and drying racks
panels.action: In a modest soap production hall, workers pour fragrant mixture into rectangular moulds and arrange drying cakes on wooden racks, sunlight slanting through high windows.

dialogue.text: The records of Karnataka Soaps later traced these beginnings: a princely state learning to move from raw material to finished good under its own name.

i18n.hi: बाद में कर्नाटक सॉप्स के रिकॉर्ड ने इन्हीं शुरुआतों को जोड़ा – एक रियासत जो कच्चे माल से तैयार माल तक अपना नाम लेकर पहुँचना सीख रही थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of both figures examining a bar of soap and a bottle of oil in an office
panels.action: In a bright office, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV holds up a finished bar of soap thoughtfully while Visvesvaraya examines a labelled bottle of sandalwood oil; samples of other products and reports lie on the table between them.

dialogue.text: These were not the works of one man alone. They rested on chemists, accountants, clerks, and a king willing to sign budgets for unseen returns.

i18n.hi: ये काम सिर्फ़ एक आदमी के नहीं थे – इनके पीछे केमिस्ट, मुनीम, क्लर्क और ऐसा राजा था जो अनदेखे लाभों के लिए भी बजट पर दस्तख़त कर देता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a nascent industrial town with a tall smokestack and railway siding
panels.action: An industrial landscape shows the Mysore Iron Works at Bhadravathi in the distance, with a tall smokestack, railway siding, and rows of workers’ quarters, as a train puffs slowly past.

dialogue.text: At Bhadravathi, Mysore Iron Works turned local ore and imported know-how into steel, anchoring a new town and a new class of skilled labour.

i18n.hi: भद्रावती में मैसूर आयरन वर्क्स ने स्थानीय अयस्क और बाहर की तकनीक से इस्पात ढाला – एक नए कसबे और नई कुशल मज़दूर बस्ती की नींव रखी।

panels.shot: interior shot of an early bank hall with counters and ledgers
panels.action: Inside a high-ceilinged banking hall, clerks sit behind wooden counters handling coins and currency, while customers in turbans and coats sign forms; ledgers labelled ‘State Bank of Mysore’ rest on stands.

dialogue.text: Finance followed industry. Institutions like the State Bank of Mysore gathered scattered savings into capital, under the state’s watchful but not suffocating hand.

i18n.hi: उद्योग के साथ पैसा भी आया – स्टेट बैंक ऑफ मैसूर जैसे संस्थान ने बिखरी बचतों को पूँजी बना कर इकट्ठा किया, राज्य की चौकस पर दम न घोंटने वाली निगरानी में।

panels.shot: medium shot of a polytechnic workshop classroom with young men at machines
panels.action: In a polytechnic workshop, young men operate lathes and drill presses under an instructor’s supervision, chalk diagrams of gears and circuits covering the wall behind them.

dialogue.text: Polytechnics and technical schools supplied fitters, draughtsmen and supervisors; chambers of commerce gave merchants a common voice to meet the state’s plans with their own.

i18n.hi: पॉलीटेक्निक और टेक्निकल स्कूलों ने फ़िटर, ड्राफ़्ट्समैन और सुपरवाइज़र दिए; चेंबर ऑफ कॉमर्स ने व्यापारियों को एक मंच दिया, ताकि वे राज्य की योजनाओं से बराबरी की बातचीत कर सकें।

panels.shot: medium shot of both in a modest conference room with charts pinned up
panels.action: In a plainer meeting room than the palace hall, walls lined with pinned charts of production, enrollment and revenue, the Maharaja and Visvesvaraya review a printed report together.

dialogue.text: Visvesvaraya wrote and spoke openly of his programme. In ‘Reconstructing India’, he argued not for miracles, but for steady systems that rewarded effort and punished waste.

i18n.hi: विश्वेश्वरैया ने अपना कार्यक्रम खुल कर लिखा और बोला – ‘रिकन्स्ट्रक्टिंग इंडिया’ में उन्होंने चमत्कार नहीं, मेहनत को इनाम और फ़िज़ूलखर्ची को सज़ा देने वाली ठोस व्यवस्थाएँ मांगीं।

panels.shot: close-up of a printed page of 'Reconstructing India' with underlined lines
panels.action: A close-up of an open book titled ‘Reconstructing India’ shows neat English text, with certain lines underlined in ink, a hand resting nearby as if in mid-study.

dialogue.text: He insisted that education, banks, factories and roads should fit together like gears, each turning the other, each accountable to public scrutiny.

i18n.hi: वे ज़िद करते रहे कि स्कूल, बैंक, फैक्ट्री और सड़कें गियर की तरह जुड़ें – एक दूसरे को घुमाएँ, और सब जनता की नज़र में जवाबदेह रहें।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of both standing on a balcony overlooking city lights at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV and Visvesvaraya stand on a high balcony, the city below lit by scattered lamps and the faint glow of factories, their silhouettes quiet against a darkening sky.

dialogue.speaker: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV
dialogue.text: May Mysore be remembered not for her battles, but for her institutions.

i18n.hi: मैसूर को उसकी लड़ाइयों से नहीं, उसकी संस्थाओं से याद किया जाए।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of modern India faintly echoing earlier panels
panels.action: A subtle montage shows a present-day university campus, a modern factory line producing soap, a steel plant, and a busy bank lobby, echoing the compositions of earlier Mysore scenes.

dialogue.text: Today, when universities multiply and factories rise across India, the Mysore of 1912–1923 recalls a quieter lesson: that lasting prosperity is built not on a single hero, but on systems where knowledge and industry grow together.

i18n.hi: आज जब भारत भर में यूनिवर्सिटियाँ और फ़ैक्ट्रियाँ बढ़ रही हैं, १९१२–२३ का मैसूर हमें शांत सबक देता है – टिकाऊ समृद्धि किसी अकेले नायक पर नहीं, ऐसे तंत्रों पर टिकती है जहाँ ज्ञान और उद्योग साथ‑साथ बढ़ते हैं।

title_i18n.en: Mysore Builds a University and Factories

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Princely Court Became a Laboratory of Learning and Steel
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक राजदरबार सीख और इस्पात की प्रयोगशाला बना
